About UsWe make the business of games work for the people who make them.rcp is an independent production house from Munich, around since 2005. Part dealmaker, part production house, part backer. We sit on the business side of the table for a family of 15 partner studios across Europe, South America and South Asia, so they can spend their time making games. When our studios win, we win.What that looks like day to day:• We sell our studios’ games and teams to publishers and platforms• We structure deals, funding and investment• We broker co-development, porting and work-for-hire• We build serious games for finance, health and defenseMore than 300 games and interactive projects so far, from Songs of Silence and Bus Simulator to Angry Birds Epic and Ostwind.Where we’re going We’re building something the games industry doesn’t have yet: a 'United Artists' for game makers. Studios that own their work, share the upside and back each other.rcp has a strong reputation and a weak brand. For you, that’s room: you get to put your own stamp on it.How we work• Roles, not positions. Inspired by holacracy. One person often holds several roles, and roles change as the work changes• Strikeforces. Small cross-functional teams around a partner studio or a mission, with clear accountability for each role• Radical candor. We care personally and challenge directly. You get honest feedback, and we expect you to give it, including to the CEO• AI-second, human-first. Coordination and admin go to AI, so people spend their time on judgment, relationships and dealsYour role: Remote (Europe or North America, on European hours) or Munich · Full-time · Exclusive freelance start possible, then permanentThe short version We need a dealmaker who opens doors at the top table and brings the close home. You take over the relationships our CEO built over 20 years, and you build your own. No team to manage. A direct line to the CEO.Why this role exists Our CEO built rcp’s top relationships over 20 years. We want someone to take them over, grow them, and become the face of rcp at the top table.You open doors at Director and VP level. You bring opportunities that hold up. You bring the close home without giving terms away early. A door-opener with soft leads doesn’t help us. A door-opener who closes does.This is a director-level role as an individual contributor. You don’t manage a team. You work directly with our CEO, our Biz team and the studio heads across the rcp family.Your responsibilities will include:• Open doors at the right level: Director and VP+ at large publishers and platforms, CEO level at smaller publishers, plus project financiers, games investors and fast-growing self-publishing developers• Pitch and sell projects from the rcp family: original IP, co-development and work-for-hire• Hold terms to the close. When a deal doesn’t fit, rethink it instead of forcing it• Own our presence at D.I.C.E., GDC and Gamescom: the plan, the meetings, the follow-ups• Take over and grow our relationships with first-party platforms, major publishers and tool providers• Be the senior sparring partner for our Biz team: review deal rationales, mentor, keep commitments visible• Bring what you hear in the market back into the groupYour profile:• A seat in the circles where games deals happen: D.I.C.E., GamesBeat, or their equivalents in LA and Asia. Established, or clearly on your way in• Relationships at Director or VP level and above, across more than one segment: publishers, platforms, investors or tool providers• At least one deal in the last three years that you originated or led to the close• A confident presence in front of C-level. Quick and sharp• Drive. You set your own goals and get things done through people, without direct reports• Readiness to travel a lot, and the energy to enjoy it• A real feel for entertainment. You play games• Business-fluent English. German is a bonusNice to have:• Experience with funding, licensing or joint ventures• You’ve sat on both sides of the table, developer and publisher• You’ve worked in an owner-led company• You already use AI for research, prep and follow-upsWho this is not for• You want to build and lead a team from day one• You need a big brand behind you to get a meeting• You’d rather have a clear job description than build somethingAbout usTo find out more about remote control productions go to our website: www.rcp.familyand sign up for our newsletter !What we offer:• Real influence: a direct line to the CEO and a voice in group strategy• Where it can go: stay the face of rcp, lead one of our partner studios, or help make our own games• Fixed pay, no commission. You’re paid to build the right deals, not to push the most deals through• A family of game makers across three continents• Munich or remote: work from our office in the heart of Munich, or remotely from Europe or North America on European hours. Permanent employment or freelance, whichever fits you and your country• Health coaching with OLAO HEALTH. In Munich: Deutschlandticket, a games library and team events

jobs.occupation: System Specialist for Incoming Material Quality & Reliability (IMQR) (m/f/d) (Qualitätskontrolleur/in)
jobs.description: Build Europe's semiconductor future with us!European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. By setting up advanced web-based systems, building key interfaces with suppliers, and shaping our quality processes from day one, your footprint will be embedded in every microchip we manufacture. If you love precision and thrive in an environment where you can actively build the structures you work with, this is your stage.Job Responsibilities• Set up and optimize our advanced web-based IMQR systems and establish automated data transfer protocols with global suppliers from the ground up.• Take ownership of material usage decisions and master data maintenance within SAP, ensuring a continuous, in-time supply of premium materials into the Fab.• Collect raw data and monitor Statistical Process Control (SPC) charts, transforming it into strategic operational workflows.• Act as the first point of contact for troubleshooting. Train internal teams as well as external international suppliers on our systems.• Collaborate closely with engineering teams to systematically improve productivity through optimized data management.Your profile• A completed vocational training (Berufsausbildung), paired with 2–5 years of professional experience in a comparable quality, data, or technical role within an international high-tech environment.• Solid expertise in data management, reporting, and ERP systems (ideally SAP), combined with a good understanding of Statistical Process Control (SPC) systems.• You thrive in dynamic, fast-paced environments and view evolving processes as an opportunity to actively shape workflows. Detail-focused. Highly resilient.• Fluent in English (our company language and communication to colleagues in Taiwan and Arizona).• Experience in a high-tech manufacturing industry. Plus, basic language skills in German or Mandarin to ease local and global collaboration.• Ready for Training at TSMC in Taiwan for 6 months.Reasons to join ESMC• Security & Perspective: A permanent employment contract and career advancement opportunities in one of Europe's leading semiconductors fabs.• Company Pension Plan & Financial Benefits : We support your financial well-being with our robust company pension plan. As an ESMC employee, you also benefit directly from TSMC’s performance through an exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).• Relocation Support for Dresden: Moving for us? We’ll provide you with all the support you will need for your relocation and your start in Dresden.• Training & Development: Depending on your position, you will gain a deeper understanding of the processes involved in operating complex semiconductor equipment through unique hands-on training at the TSMC Newcomer Training Center, while continuously expanding your knowledge.• Health & Well-Being: An annual budget for your health and well-being (e.g., for sports classes, massages, or relaxation) helps you stay fit.• Meals & Transportation: Enjoy a daily meal allowance as well as a subsidized public transportation (e.g., for the Deutschlandticket) in Germany.Application documentsPlease apply with your English CV.About usEach journey starts with a first step.Joining ESMC at this early stage will provide you with the unique opportunity to actively shape the future of the fab in Dresden, boost your career and put your true potential to the test. You will be working in a fast paced, international startup environment whilst at the same time having access to the experience, talent, and resources of the largest and most advanced semiconductor manufacturer in the world, TSMC. You have ample opportunities to learn about TSMC Operations, Digital Transformation, and various advanced Facilities related topics, both in Taiwan and other sites around the world.Behind the world’s most advanced technology are real people with real passion. Our success is fueled by our core values: Integrity, Commitment, Innovation and Customer Trust (ICIC).We create a work environment that promotes diversity, ignites passion and enables you to reach your full potential.At ESMC, we welcome applications from all people, regardless of race, ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual identity.

jobs.occupation: Wissenschaftl. Mitarbeiter*in (w/m/d) Metabarcoding-Datenkuratierung u. Bioinformatik Kennz18/2026/2 (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Das Leibniz-Institut für Gartenbauwissenschaften (IGZ) betreibt exzellente pflanzenwissenschaftliche Grundlagenforschung für die Anwendung im Gartenbau mit Schwerpunkt Gemüse und der Nutzung pflanzlicher Diversität.  Das IGZ ist Teil der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft und hat seinen Sitz in Großbeeren.  Weitere Informationen finden Sie auf unserer Webseite: www.igzev.de.Im Institut ist ab dem 01.02.2027, befristet für zwei Jahre, in der Forschungsgruppe „System Pflanze-Mikroorganismen“ im Rahmen des DFG-geförderten Verbundvorhaben „Vielschichtiger Datenkorpus für KI Anwendungen in der Mikrobiellen Ökologie“ (MuCoME, Förderung im Rahmen „Wissenschaftliche Literaturversorgungs- und Informationssysteme“ (LIS) der DFG) folgende Stelle zu besetzen:Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiterin (w,m,div.) im Bereich Metabarcoding-Datenkuratierung und BioinformatikKennz.  18/2026/2Die Vergütung erfolgt entsprechend der Qualifikation und Erfahrung nach dem Tarifvertrag TV–L, bis zur Entgeltgruppe 13, in Teilzeit mit 80% der regulären Arbeitszeit.Das Projekt erweitert die Microbial Community Database (MiCoDa, https://micoda.idiv.de/) zu einem umfassenden, KI-tauglichen Datenkorpus für die mikrobielle Metabarcoding-Forschung.  Gemeinsam mit Partnern am IOW (Warnemünde) und der Hochschule Wismar werden Methoden zur Extraktion und Harmonisierung unstrukturierter Metadaten aus Publikationen sowie zur Kuratierung und Harmonisierung von 16S rRNA-Metabarcoding-Sequenzdaten entwickelt, mit dem Ziel, MiCoDa auf mindestens 200.000 Proben zu erweitern und den öffentlichen Zugang über MiCoDa, GBIF und ENA zu verbessern.Die Aufgaben umfassen- Zusammenstellung eines Referenzdatensatzes aus 16S rRNA-Gen-Metabarcoding-Daten von Mock-Communities aus INSDC-Datenbanken sowie durch strukturierte Literaturrecherche- Untersuchung, wie technische Entscheidungen die Vergleichbarkeit archivierter Datensätze beeinflussen- Automatisierung der Kuratierung und Harmonisierung von Metabarcoding-Daten- Anleitung und Betreuung einer studentischen Hilfskraft bei der Datenkuratierung- Mitwirkung an der Kommunikation mit der European Nucleotide Archive- Verfassen wissenschaftlicher Publikationen in internationalen Fachzeitschriften mit Peer-Review und Präsentation der Ergebnisse auf KonferenzenIhr Profil- eine abgeschlossene Promotion mit bioinformatischem Schwerpunkt oder einem verwandten naturwissenschaftlichen Fach- Erfahrung in der bioinformatischen Analyse von 16S rRNA-Metabarcoding-Daten (z.B. dada2) und im Umgang mit öffentlichen Sequenzarchiven (ENA/INSDC)- Erfahrung mit statistischen Analysen (idealerweise gemischte Modelle) und mit Hochleistungsrechenumgebungen- Programmierkenntnisse (R und/oder Python) sowie idealerweise Erfahrung mit Workflow-Management- verhandlungssichere englische Sprachkenntnisse; Kenntnisse der deutschen Sprache sind von Vorteil- eine offene, flexible und positive Person, die in einem interdisziplinären, internationalen Team arbeiten kann, aber auch in der Lage ist, die Initiative zu ergreifenWir bieten- einen attraktiven Arbeitsplatz an einem modernen Forschungsinstitut für Gartenbauwissenschaften- ein engagiertes und kompetentes Team und eine anspruchsvolle Tätigkeit an der Schnittstelle von Bioinformatik, Datenmanagement und mikrobieller Ökologie- die Einbindung in ein Konsortium mit Partnern am IOW und der Hochschule Wismar sowie Anschluss an die NFDI-Konsortien 4Biodiversity und 4Microbiota- flexible und familiengerechte Arbeitszeitmodelle und die Möglichkeit des mobilen Arbeitens (bis zu 50% der Arbeitszeit)- VBL Ost-betriebliche Altersvorsorge im öffentlichen Dienst sowie tarifliche Jahressonderzahlung und 30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr- Zuschuss zum Firmenticket für den öffentlichen Nahverkehr oder zum DeutschlandticketRückfragen sind möglich bei Dr. Stephanie Jurburg (jurburg@igzev.de).Wir fördern die Vereinbarkeit von Beruf, Familie und Pflege und setzen uns für Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt ein.  Menschen mit Behinderung werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt.  Wir begrüßen Bewerbungen unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, sexueller Orientierung, Religion, Weltanschauung oder ethnischer Herkunft.Bitte senden Sie Ihre vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen bestehend aus einem Motivationsschreiben, Ihrem Lebenslauf und Kopien von akademischen Zeugnissen inkl. der Angabe Ihres frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermins und der Nennung von zwei Referenzen bis zum 22.11.2026 unter Angabe der Kennziffer in einem PDF-Dokument an bewerbung@igzev.de._________________________________________________________________________________________________________________Leibniz Institute for Horticultural Sciences (IGZ) conducts excellent basic research in plant sciences with applications in horticulture focusing on vegetables and the use of plant diversity. The IGZ is a member of the Leibniz Association and is based in Grossbeeren. For further information, please visit our website: www.igzev.de (https://igzev.de/en/home) .The following position is available at the institute from February 1, 2027 for a fixed term of two years in the research group ‘Plant-Microbe Systems’ within the DFG-funded collaborative project 'Multi-level Corpus for Microbial Ecology' (MuCoME, funded within the Scientific Library Services and Information Systems (LIS) programme of the DFG):Postdoctoral Researcher (f, m, div.) in the Field of Metabarcoding Data Curation and BioinformaticsReference number: 18/2026/2The salary will be based on qualification and research experience according to the wage agreement TV-L, up to pay scale 13, 80% of regular working hours.The project expands the Microbial Community Database (MiCoDa, https://micoda.idiv.de/) into a comprehensive, AI-ready data corpus for microbial metabarcoding research. Together with partners at IOW (Warnemünde) and Hochschule Wismar, the project develops methods for extracting and harmonising unstructured metadata from publications, as well as for curating and harmonising 16S rRNA metabarcoding sequence data, aiming to expand MiCoDa to at least 200,000 samples (v3) and improve public access via MiCoDa, GBIF, and ENA.Tasks include- compiling a reference dataset of 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding mock community data from INSDC databases and through structured literature searches- examining how technical choices affect the comparability of archived datasets- automating curation and harmonization of metabarcoding data- supervising a student assistant in data curation tasks- writing scientific publications in peer-reviewed international journals and presenting results at conferences- contributing to communication with the European Nucleotide ArchiveYour profile- a completed PhD with a focus on bioinformatics or a related natural science field- experience in the bioinformatic analysis of 16S rRNA metabarcoding data (e.g. dada2) and working with public sequence archives (ENA/INSDC)- experience with statistical analyses (ideally mixed-effects models) and with high-performance computing environments- programming skills (R and/or Python) and ideally experience with workflow management- fluent English language skills; knowledge of German is an advantage- an open, flexible and positive person who can work in an interdisciplinary, international team but is also able to take the initiativeWe offer - an attractive workplace at a modern research institute for horticultural sciences- a committed and competent team and a challenging position at the interface of bioinformatics, data management, and microbial ecology- integration into a consortium with partners at IOW and Hochschule Wismar, as well as connections to the NFDI4Biodiversity and NFDI4Microbiota consortia- flexible and family-friendly working time models and the possibility of mobile working (up to 50% of working time)- VBL Ost company pension scheme for public sector employees, as well as a collectively agreed annual bonus and 30 days' vacation per year- subsidy for the company ticket for local public transport or for the Deutschland-TicketFor questions, please contact: Dr. Stephanie Jurburg (jurburg@igzev.de (witzel@igzev.de) ).We support the reconciliation of work, family and caring responsibilities and are committed to equal opportunities and diversity.
